goal: Lily (drawn young, about five years old) stands next to Grandpa in a bright living room with a green sofa and a window and points at him; Grandpa holds a newspaper. No letters, words, or numbers anywhere.

Picture 3 is the empty living room of Lily: warm cream walls, a light wooden floor, a green sofa with two cushions, a window with cream curtains at the right of the sofa, a small round side table with a lamp at the left, and a plain round rug; use it as the background and keep the same room. Picture 4 shows one plain folded newspaper that is plain blank cream paper with no print at all (no letters, no lines, no photos). Keep the soft, round, bright 3D render look of the pictures, not a 2D drawing and no outlines. The children keep their chibi proportions: a big head and a small body; the adults keep the adult proportions of their pictures (about one and a half times as tall as the five-year-old children; Tom, who is eight, is a little taller than Lily). Hands are small, clean hands with five clear short fingers (four fingers and one thumb) when open, never fists unless stated, and a hanging hand shows relaxed, separate short fingers. Do not change anyone's skin tone, hair, or clothes. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no writing on any picture or sign. The picture is for young children and is rated G. Keep each character exactly as in the pictures: Lily: a girl of five with a short dark-brown bob with a straight fringe and one small lilac bow at the side of her hair, big brown eyes, a lilac dress with short sleeves and a small white collar, white socks, pink shoes; Grandpa: an older man, a little shorter than Dad, with short white hair and a small white mustache, a green knitted cardigan over a white shirt, brown trousers, brown shoes. Grandpa stands at the right of the picture and Lily stands beside him at the middle of the picture, both full-body in view. Lily faces the camera, smiles a big smile, and points at Grandpa with the index finger of one hand; her other hand hangs relaxed. Grandpa faces the camera, smiles warmly, and holds ONE folded newspaper (picture 4: plain blank cream paper, with no print at all, no letters, no lines, no photos) in one hand at his side; his other hand hangs relaxed. The green sofa and the window are soft behind them. Exactly two people: Lily and Grandpa. Exactly the characters named here are in the picture, and no other person or animal. A character of the pictures that this description does not name must not appear. Every named character has a clear, whole, friendly face. The page text is "This is my grandpa." and is context only: do not draw any text.
linePrompt: Picture 1 is a 3D-rendered children's book picture. Convert picture 1 to line art for a student book: thick, even black lines (about three times a normal outline), simple closed shapes that a 5-year-old can color, on pure white. No blush circles, no eyelash ticks, no hair strands, no shading, no gray, no texture lines, no text. Keep every shape in the same place and the same size. Draw each eye as a closed outline with a big solid black pupil (a filled black circle) inside it. Draw the mouth exactly as in picture 1: an open mouth stays an open mouth drawn as a closed outline, and a closed smile stays one curve. Draw each hand as a closed outline with each finger as a separate rounded shape. Each head of hair is one closed shape. The ear is one closed outline with at most one inner curve. No lines on the clothes other than the outline, the collar, the cuffs, the buttons, and the star. No wrinkle lines on any face. Simplify the background: draw only a few large, simple, closed shapes (the floor line, the wall line, the window as one closed rectangle with its curtain as one closed shape, the sofa as one closed shape with each cushion as one closed shape, the rug as one closed oval, the side table, the lamp, and the toy box as simple closed shapes). No wood grain lines, no floor plank lines, no wall texture, no hatching, no tick marks, no small details. Every outline is one closed line that never runs into a background line; no loose line ends anywhere. Every line inside an object ends on another line. Use few background shapes. Grandma's curly hair is one closed cloud-like shape with no strands; Grandpa's mustache is one closed shape; draw no wrinkle lines. The newspaper is one closed folded-paper shape with one fold line; nothing is drawn on it.
